name: Ice-Fish Boat Breathing (Băng Ngư Thuyền Tức Pháp)
concept: The outer disciples' method, practised at the oars. The rower breathes with the stroke and draws the river's Water qi in on the pull and down on the return, so that a day's rowing is a day's cultivation. It is a working method for people who must work, and the Liên Giang fishers say it is the only công pháp that pays for itself.
lore: Lư Độc Điếu wrote it down in 1140 from the way his grandfather rowed, so the school could take boat children who had no time to sit.

name: Lone Line Sitting Canon (Độc Điếu Tọa Kinh)
concept: The school's attempt to revive Hàn Giang Môn's ice-hole cultivation (A128). The cultivator cuts a hole in the river ice, drops a line, and sits beside it in the snow without moving, drawing the cold river's qi up the line and into the body for days at a time. It is a patient Water method: it builds a deep pool of linh lực and a ward that thickens while the holder is Composed. Because it was pieced together from old fishers' memories, its last layers are uncertain, and the eighth is where its disciples stall.
lore: Lư Độc Điếu built it between 1120 and 1140 from what Bồ Tọa Tuyết and the last old sitters of Liên Giang remembered. The true manual of Hàn Giang Môn is lost, as far as the school knows.
